name: Capecitabine
route_note: oral tablets twice daily, typically 14 days on and 7 days off
originator: Nippon Roche (Kamakura Research Laboratories) / Hoffmann-La Roche
owner: generic (many); Xeloda brand held by Roche

discovery.note: Designed as a three-step prodrug to generate 5-FU preferentially in tumour tissue rich in thymidine phosphorylase.

tagline: Oral prodrug that converts to fluorouracil inside tumours
summary: Capecitabine is an orally absorbed prodrug converted to fluorouracil through three enzymatic steps, the last catalysed by thymidine phosphorylase, which is often elevated in tumours. It is used in colorectal, breast, gastric and pancreatic cancer and can replace infusional 5-FU in many regimens.
mechanism: After absorption, hepatic carboxylesterase converts capecitabine to 5′-deoxy-5-fluorocytidine; cytidine deaminase then forms 5′-deoxy-5-fluorouridine; thymidine phosphorylase finally releases 5-fluorouracil.
The released 5-FU acts as a thymidylate synthase inhibitor and is misincorporated into RNA and DNA. Clearance depends on dihydropyrimidine dehydrogenase, so DPD deficiency causes serious toxicity.
uses: Adjuvant and metastatic colorectal cancer (alone or as CAPOX)
Metastatic breast cancer (alone or with docetaxel); residual disease after neoadjuvant therapy

history.title: Design
history.detail: Prodrug programme at Nippon Roche identifies capecitabine.

history.title: FDA approval
history.detail: Approved as Xeloda for metastatic breast cancer resistant to paclitaxel and anthracyclines.

history.title: Colorectal cancer
history.detail: FDA approves first-line use in metastatic colorectal cancer.

history.title: Adjuvant colon
history.detail: X-ACT shows oral capecitabine is at least equivalent to bolus 5-FU/leucovorin in stage III colon cancer; FDA approves adjuvant use.

history.title: Generics
history.detail: Generic capecitabine launches in the US.

history.title: CREATE-X
history.detail: Adjuvant capecitabine improves survival in HER2-negative breast cancer with residual disease after neoadjuvant chemotherapy.

history.title: Label modernisation
history.detail: FDA updates the Xeloda label through Project Renewal, removing the former boxed warning on warfarin interaction.

pk.metabolism: carboxylesterase, cytidine deaminase, thymidine phosphorylase; DPD catabolism of 5-FU

facts: Its tumour selectivity relies on higher thymidine phosphorylase activity in many tumours than in normal tissue.
